nvidia-delay-truth-reconciliation.answer: Status: unresolved (claim vs corporate denial). The original claim comes from research firm SemiAnalysis (X post + report, July 5-6, 2026): NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale system for Rubin Ultra slipped from 2027 to 2028 because the PCB midplane — a key circuit board — remains hard to manufacture, with the larger NVL576 also likely delayed. stripe-webhook-secret-rotation-runbook.answer: Safest documented procedure to rotate a Stripe webhook signing secret: (1) In the Dashboard, open Workbench → Webhooks tab, click the endpoint whose secret you want to roll. (2) Open the overflow menu and click 'Roll secret'. (3) Choose delayed expiration (up to 24 hours) rather than immediate expiry — during that window multiple secrets are active and Stripe generates one signature per secret, giving you overlap to deploy the new secret to your server without dropping events. (4) Update the endpoint secret in your server config/secret manager (never commit it — Stripe's own sample warns 'Don't put any keys in code'), deploy, and verify signature verification succeeds using official libraries against the Stripe-Signature header before the old secret expires. Rollback within the window = keep verifying with the old secret (still active until expiry). There is no dedicated 'roll' API endpoint documented on this page; the documented path is the Dashboard/Workbench flow.

data.procedure: Workbench → Webhooks tab → select endpoint → overflow menu → Roll secret → choose expiration (immediate or up to 24h delay) → update server-side endpoint secret → verify signatures → old secret expires
data.overlapBehavior: Expiration of the old secret can be delayed up to 24 hours; during that time multiple secrets are active for the endpoint and Stripe generates one signature per secret until expiration
data.verificationStep: Verify webhook signatures with Stripe's official libraries using the endpoint secret and the Stripe-Signature header (raw request body required); confirm 2xx deliveries in the endpoint's Event deliveries tab
data.doNotCommit: The webhook signing secret (whsec_...) and API keys — keep out of code/VCS per Stripe's 'Don't put any keys in code' guidance

do-google-dns-certbot-migration-plan.answer: Migration checklist for moving A records in Google Cloud DNS to the DigitalOcean Reserved IP and then issuing nginx certs with certbot. PRE-CUTOVER: (1) verify the Reserved IP answers: curl -sI -H 'Host: avantimediagroup.com' http://45.55.116.209 (expect 200 from the intended droplet); (2) record current DNS: dig +short A avantimediagroup.com www.avantimediagroup.com scripts.avantimediagroup.com avantfutures.com www.avantfutures.com @8.8.8.8; (3) lower TTL if needed. DNS CHANGE (Google Cloud DNS, per record): gcloud dns record-sets update avantimediagroup.com. --rrdatas=45.55.116.209 --ttl=300 --type=A --zone=ZONE (repeat for the other four names, or use the Cloud DNS console Edit flow). Reserved IPs are static and reassignable between droplets, which is exactly why DNS should target the reserved IP, not the droplet's ephemeral IP. POST-CUTOVER VERIFY: dig +short A <each name> @8.8.8.8 returns 45.55.116.209; curl -I http://<name> serves the droplet. TLS: on the droplet run sudo certbot --nginx (certbot requires the site already online over HTTP port 80, which is why certs come AFTER the DNS cutover); verify with curl -I https://avantimediagroup.com and sudo certbot renew --dry-run.

data.dnsChange: In Google Cloud DNS, update the A record-sets for avantimediagroup.com, www.avantimediagroup.com, scripts.avantimediagroup.com, avantfutures.com, www.avantfutures.com from 138.197.113.36 to the DigitalOcean Reserved IP 45.55.116.209 via `gcloud dns record-sets update NAME --rrdatas=45.55.116.209 --ttl=300 --type=A --zone=ZONE` (or console Edit)
data.verificationCommands: BEFORE: dig +short A avantimediagroup.com @8.8.8.8; curl -sI -H 'Host: avantimediagroup.com' http://45.55.116.209 | head -1. AFTER: for h in avantimediagroup.com www.avantimediagroup.com scripts.avantimediagroup.com avantfutures.com www.avantfutures.com; do dig +short A $h @8.8.8.8; done; curl -I https://avantimediagroup.com; sudo certbot renew --dry-run

local-cli-plus-web-dns-audit.answer: DNS audit result: ALL FIVE hostnames are mispointed. Local dig probes (@8.8.8.8) show avantimediagroup.com, www.avantimediagroup.com, scripts.avantimediagroup.com, avantfutures.com, and www.avantfutures.com each resolving to 138.197.113.36 — the destroyed droplet's recycled IP now held by a stranger ('Arcane Ledger') — instead of the intended DigitalOcean Reserved IP 45.55.116.209 (already assigned to the live droplet 192.241.255.56 and verified serving Command Center by Host header). Risk: every visitor, webhook (including Stripe), and the self-hosted ntfy endpoint is being delivered to an unrelated third party's server over the stranger's TLS cert. Reserved IPs exist precisely for this: per DigitalOcean docs they are static, reassignable addresses, so pointing DNS at the reserved IP prevents a future recycle from orphaning DNS again. Fix in Google Cloud DNS (the zone's NS is googledomains.com — NOT DigitalOcean DNS): update the five A record-sets to 45.55.116.209 via gcloud dns record-sets update, then AFTER propagation run sudo certbot --nginx on the droplet (certbot requires the site reachable over HTTP first). No DNS, Stripe, or server changes were made in this audit.
